title: Define per-tenant SLIs, traceflow, and KV-cache budget enforcement for analytics ingest pipeline
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: Our analytics ingest and processing pipeline currently exposes coarse, service-level SLIs and traces. This makes it hard to detect tenant-specific regressions (cost spikes, increased ingest latency, or KV cache thrash). Goal: Define clear, testable per-tenant SLIs (success rate, P95 processing latency, backlog size, KV cache hit ratio and cost budget burn), implement trace propagation (frontdoor -> broker -> processor -> storage) with low-cost sampling, and add automated enforcement hooks to prevent a single tenant from breaching a KV cache cost budget. Deliver dashboards, alerts, and runbooks suitable for oncall and SRE teams.
acceptance_criteria: SLI document published in playbook repo (definitions + measurement queries)
Per-tenant metrics emitted for: ingest_success_rate, processor_p95_ms, ingest_backlog_count, kv_cache_hit_ratio, kv_cache_cost_rolling_hour
Trace propagation verified end-to-end for sampled requests with tenant_id present in spans
Dashboards created (tenant overview, top offenders, cost burn heatmap) and linked in ticket
Alerts wired: P0 for >1% tenant ingest failure over 5m, P1 for processor_p95 > 2s for a tenant for 10m, P0 for kv_cache_cost_rolling_hour > tenant_budget * 1.2
Auto-mitigation workflow implemented: soft throttle + rollout to new routing policy for offending tenant, with manual override
Synthetic test harness validates traceflow and SLI collection in CI for a canary tenant
Runbook and postmortem template updated and reviewed by SRE/Oncall
instrumentation_plan: Add semantic span at frontdoor (ingest-api) including fields: trace_id, tenant_id, request_type, payload_size
Emit a span at message broker enqueue and dequeue with message_id and tenant_id
Processor service to add processing_start/end spans and metric tags: tenant_id (hashed_bucket), stage, success|failure
Storage/KV layer to emit kv_cache_hit/miss counter and per-tenant estimated cost meter (approx USD/hour equivalents)
Use hashed tenant buckets (N=4096) for high-cardinality metrics; emit direct tenant_id only for sampled traces and for tiered audit logs under enterprise contracts
Implement dynamic sampling: baseline 0.1% global, escalate to 5% for tenants who cross anomaly thresholds, while capping total trace volume
Support trace-context propagation via existing W3C traceparent headers and add tenant_id header enforcement in gateway
dashboard_and_alert_mapping: Tenant Overview: top 50 tenants by ingest volume + columns: success_rate_1h, p95_processing_ms, kv_cache_hit_ratio, kv_cost_1h
Cost Heatmap: tenant vs hour showing kv_cache_cost_rolling_hour with shading for >75% of budget
Traceflow Explorer: quick link to sampled traces filtered by tenant_id and time window
Alert rules: ingest_failure_rate > 1% triggers oncall runbook; kv_cost_rolling_hour > budget*1.2 triggers auto-throttle and PagerDuty
SLO Compliance Dashboard: historical compliance per tenant (30d) with SLA burn rate visualizations
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): instrument internal tenants only, validate metrics and traces (1 week)
Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5% production traffic (10 low-risk tenants) with increased sampling and dashboard checks (2 weeks)
Phase 2: expand to 25% production traffic and enable auto-mitigation in monitor mode (2 weeks)
Phase 3: full rollout to all tenants, enable auto-throttle policy with manual override and audit logging (1 week)
Rollback: remove tenant from sampling and disable enforcement; fallback to legacy routing policy
notes: We must be careful with cardinality — full-tenant tagged metrics will blow up storage costs. Plan uses hashed buckets and sampled full tags only for enterprise audited logs.
KV cache cost estimation will be an approximation based on per-get cost * estimated ops/sec; accuracy should be within 15% for initial rollout.
Coordination needed with Billing for tenant budget definitions and enforcement API (soft throttle should not bill dispute-sensitive operations).
